patterns.title: No function keyword
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not use the `function` keyword. Just write the name followed by (). This is the same as CoD4 GSC.

patterns.title: No var/let/const declarations
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no variable declaration keywords. All variables are dynamically typed — just assign them.

patterns.title: No ternary operator
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support the ternary operator ?:. Use if/else.

patterns.title: No arrow functions
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support arrow functions (=>). Use named functions or inline for loops.

patterns.title: No template literals
patterns.right: msg = "Hello " + self.name + ", you have " + self.score + " points";
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support template literals (backticks). Use + for string concatenation.

patterns.title: No .push() — use indexed append
patterns.right: myArray[myArray.size] = newItem;
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC arrays have no .push() method. Append by assigning to the index equal to .size.

patterns.title: No .length — use .size
patterns.right: count = myArray.size;
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC uses .size (not .length) to get the number of elements in an array or string.

patterns.title: Iterating arrays — use indexed for loop
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support for...of iteration. Always use an indexed for loop with .size.

patterns.title: No array destructuring
patterns.right:
first = myArray[0];
second = myArray[1];
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support destructuring assignment. Access array elements by index individually.

patterns.title: No object literals — use spawnstruct()
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support object literal syntax {key: value}. Create a struct with spawnstruct() then assign properties.

patterns.title: No new keyword — use spawnstruct()
patterns.right:
obj = spawnstruct();
obj.x = 5;
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not have a `new` keyword. Use spawnstruct() to create plain data objects.

patterns.title: Check property exists before accessing
patterns.right: if (isDefined(player.customData) && isDefined(player.customData.score) && player.customData.score > 0) {}
patterns.explanation: Accessing an undefined property crashes IW4. Always guard with isDefined() before accessing nested properties.

patterns.title: Deleting a property
patterns.right: player.tempData = undefined;
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no delete operator. Set the property to undefined to undefine it.

patterns.title: No null literal — use isDefined()
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not have a 'null' keyword. Use isDefined() or !isDefined() to check if a variable has a value.

patterns.title: No strict equality — use == and !=
patterns.right:
if (x == 5) {}
if (name != "allies") {}
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC does not support === or !==. Use == and != instead. All comparisons in IW4 are non-strict.

patterns.title: Converting types — use int() and float()
patterns.right:
n = int(strValue);
f = float(strValue);
patterns.explanation: Use IW4's built-in int() and float() functions for type conversion, not JavaScript's parseInt/parseFloat.

patterns.title: Math functions — use built-ins not Math.*
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no Math object. Use int() for floor, abs() for absolute value, randomfloat()/randomint() for random numbers.

patterns.title: Infinite loop pattern
patterns.explanation: Both work in IW4, but for(;;) is the conventional infinite loop idiom in GSC. Always include a wait to avoid server freezing.

patterns.title: No forEach or .map()/.filter()
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no functional array methods. Build result arrays manually with indexed for loops.

patterns.title: Always wait inside infinite loops
patterns.explanation: Any infinite loop MUST have at least one wait call per iteration. Without it, the server will freeze and disconnect all players.

patterns.title: waittill must be called on an entity
patterns.right: level waittill("connected", player);
patterns.explanation: waittill must always be prefixed with an entity (level, self, game, or a player entity). Bare waittill() is invalid.

patterns.title: waittill unpacks into local variables
patterns.right:
self waittill("damage", amount, attacker, sMeansOfDeath);
// now attacker is available
patterns.explanation: waittill() passes event data as additional local variables. List them after the event name string to capture them.

patterns.title: endon must be called on an entity
patterns.explanation: endon must always be prefixed with an entity. It terminates the current thread when the specified event fires on that entity.

patterns.title: Use thread for async operations
patterns.wrong:
// This blocks the calling function
watchAllPlayers();
patterns.right:
// This runs concurrently
level thread watchAllPlayers();
patterns.explanation: Use 'thread' to spawn non-blocking concurrent execution. Without it, the calling function is blocked until the callee returns.

patterns.title: notify broadcasts an event on an entity
patterns.right:
level notify("round_over");
// listeners: level waittill("round_over")
patterns.explanation: notify must always be called on an entity. The entity is the channel — waittill listeners on the same entity will wake up.

patterns.title: No 'this' — use 'self'
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC has no 'this' keyword. When a function is called on an entity (e.g., player damagePlayer()), use 'self' to refer to that entity.

patterns.title: Check if player is alive with isAlive()
patterns.explanation: Use isAlive() instead of checking health > 0. Players can have health > 0 while still in the dying state.

patterns.title: String concatenation with +
patterns.right: msg = "Score: " + self.score;
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC supports the + operator for string concatenation. There is no .concat() method.

patterns.title: Printing to players — use iprintln not println
patterns.explanation: println() only prints to the server console. Use iprintln() for screen messages or iprintlnbold() for bold centered messages to players.

patterns.title: Getting all players — use getplayers()
patterns.right:
players = getplayers();
for (i = 0; i < players.size; i++) {}
patterns.explanation: Always use getplayers() to get the current list of connected players. level.players may not be defined or up to date.

patterns.title: Invented HUD creation function
patterns.right:
elem = newClientHudElem(self);
elem setParent(level.uiParent);
patterns.explanation: The only valid HUD element creation function is newClientHudElem(player) for player-specific elements, or newHudElem() for all-player elements. Always call setParent(level.uiParent) immediately after.

patterns.title: Wrong shader name for solid rectangle
patterns.explanation: The built-in blank texture is named 'white'. Use setShader("white", w, h) to create a solid rectangle, then control its color via elem.color. Names like 'rect', 'fill', 'solidwhite', 'box' do not exist.

patterns.title: Wrong button input event in IW4X
patterns.explanation: In IW4X/MW2, use notifyOnPlayerCommand(eventName, "+action") to bind game actions to custom notify events, then waittill on those events. The events 'keypress', 'button_pressed', 'onButtonPress' do not exist as built-in notifies.

patterns.title: openMenu() called on a HUD script menu
patterns.explanation: openMenu() only works with compiled native .menu files registered via precacheMenu(). HUD-element menus built with newClientHudElem are opened by directly calling your custom display/init function. openMenu() on a non-existent menu name silently does nothing.

patterns.title: closeMenu() called on a HUD script menu
patterns.explanation: closeMenu() and closePopupMenu() only affect native .menu file overlays. HUD-element menus must be closed by calling destroy() on every element you created. Missing this causes ghost elements to accumulate.

patterns.title: setText() called on a shader/rect element
patterns.explanation: Elements created with newClientHudElem are for shaders/rectangles. Text must be created with self createFontString(font, scale). These are two separate element types. Calling setText() on a rect element does nothing.

patterns.title: Direct property assignment for HUD text
patterns.right: elem setText("Hello");
patterns.explanation: HUD element text is set via the setText() method, not by assigning to a .text property. Direct assignment is silently ignored.

patterns.title: Missing setParent after newClientHudElem
patterns.explanation: setParent(level.uiParent) is mandatory immediately after newClientHudElem(). Without it, the element may not render or may clip incorrectly. This is a silent failure.

patterns.title: Missing endon guards in menu thread
patterns.explanation: Menu threads run per-player. Without endon("disconnect") and endon("death"), the thread keeps running and HUD elements persist as ghosts after the player disconnects or dies. Always add both guards at the top of any player menu thread.

patterns.title: waittill menuresponse without a .menu file
patterns.explanation: The 'menuresponse' notify only fires when a compiled .menu file executes scriptMenuResponse. Pure HUD-element menus never trigger it. If you're building an HUD menu, use notifyOnPlayerCommand for input instead. If using native .menu files, call openMenu() first.

patterns.title: Invalid setPoint alignment strings
patterns.explanation: setPoint() alignment strings are uppercase compound words with no separators: TOPLEFT, TOP, TOPRIGHT, LEFT, CENTER, RIGHT, BOTTOMLEFT, BOTTOM, BOTTOMRIGHT. Hyphenated, camelCase, or lowercase variants are invalid and cause silent positioning failures.

patterns.title: Missing default case in menuresponse switch (CoD4)
patterns.explanation: In CoD4/IW3, a switch statement on a menuresponse value without a default: case will crash the script if an unexpected response arrives. Always include default: break; in menuresponse switch blocks.

patterns.title: wait 0 in button polling loop
patterns.explanation: wait 0 yields for exactly one server frame but provides no debounce for button input. In tight menu loops this can cause multiple triggers per button press or contribute to server freezes. Use wait 0.05 (50ms) as a minimum debounce delay after acting on input.

patterns.title: HUD elements not destroyed on menu close
patterns.explanation: HUD elements created with newClientHudElem and createFontString persist until explicitly destroyed. Failing to call destroy() on each element when closing the menu causes them to remain visible on screen and accumulate across menu opens. Always destroy every element in your close/cleanup function.

patterns.title: Invalid font name on HUD text element
patterns.right:
elem.font = "default";
// Other valid names: bigfixed, smallfixed, hudfixed, objective, big, small
patterns.explanation: IW4 GSC only supports a fixed set of engine font names: default, bigfixed, smallfixed, hudfixed, objective, big, small. Arbitrary font names like 'Arial' silently fall back to the default font or cause errors. There is no way to load custom fonts.

patterns.title: HUD color set as a string instead of a vector
patterns.right:
elem.color = (1, 0, 0); // red
elem.color = (0, 0, 0); // black
elem.color = (1, 1, 1); // white
patterns.explanation: elem.color must be a 3-component GSC vector (R, G, B) with values from 0.0 to 1.0. String values are silently ignored. Parentheses in GSC denote a vector literal, not a function call.

patterns.title: notifyOnPlayerCommand used in CoD4/IW3
patterns.explanation: notifyOnPlayerCommand() is an IW4/MW2 function. It does NOT exist in stock CoD4 (IW3). In CoD4, button detection for menus requires a compiled .menu file with execKey/scriptMenuResponse, and GSC listens via waittill('menuresponse',...). CoD4X (the community client) backports notifyOnPlayerCommand, so it works there.

patterns.title: openMenu() without precacheMenu() in init
patterns.wrong:
// During gameplay, no prior precache:
self openMenu(game["myMenu"]); // silently fails or crashes
patterns.explanation: Native .menu files must be registered with precacheMenu(game["menuName"]) during the init phase (before the game starts / in onPlayerConnect) before they can be opened. Calling openMenu() for an unregistered menu silently does nothing or causes a script error.
